articleTitle: S-Cane: Ultrasonic Sensor-Based Smart Cane for the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: One out of six people in the world suffers from disabilities, including physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory impairments. The disability hinders their participation in society and limits their access to education, healthcare, and employment. Among disabilities, visual impairment requires assistive equipment such as white canes. Conventional canes have limitations in obstacle detection and may not address concerns such as potholes. Information and communication technology have been explored in numerous studies to enhance the usability of white canes for the blind. In this study, a low-cost smart cane called S-Cane was developed, aiming to detect obstacles, water pools, and potholes, with an emphasis on affordability and ease of manufacturing. A usability test was performed on a visually impaired user. The experiment results presented a detection error with an RMSE of 0.617 and a SUS score of 77.5. The results suggest that S-Cane has a tolerable detection error and sufficient usability.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology for Privacy Protection in Healthcare Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: This study proposes establishing a model for patient data privacy protection, considering the numerous potential breaches beyond the data owner’s control in response to the rapid growth of the Indonesian healthcare industry, bolstered by technological advancements. With its immutable nature, enhanced security features, and potential for peer-to-peer distribution, blockchain technology is uniquely positioned to revolutionize healthcare data management. By creating a blockchain-based model, this research aims to elucidate the necessity of data owner consent for data entry and alterations, ensuring transparent recording for the data owners. Furthermore, it seeks to safeguard the data flow, thus presenting the potential to serve as a national benchmark for data privacy in the Indonesian health sector.

articleTitle: Automated Detection and Modeling for the Removal of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation Artifacts
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a noninvasive method that can mimic invasive vagus nerve stimulation to treat epilepsy and can significantly reduce symptoms of major depressive disorder (MDD). However, further investigation of the effect of taVNS in clinical applications remains warranted because the taVNS field is still in its infancy. Electroencephalography (EEG) can provide valuable insight into brain activity and serve as a biomarker for assessing taVNS-induced brain arousal. However, taVNS poses challenges in EEG analysis owing to the possibility of electrical current interference with the EEG signals. We proposed a novel approach to address taVNS artifacts during EEG recording. Our aim is to analyze the EEG during the taVNS effect by modeling the artifact and subtracting it from the EEG recording. With 40 taVNS sessions administered before, during, or after the puzzle task, we demonstrated the successful removal of the taVNS artifact while maintaining the EOG artifact. This artifact removal method will enable taVNS analysis in EEG during stimulation, effectively demonstrating the effect of taVNS on cortical activity.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Diabetic Foot Ulcers: Deep Learning Classification using Thermograms (AlexNet Algorithm)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate and improve the performance of AlexNet algorithm in classifying diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) through thermograms. Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is one of the chronic and common illness on the planet. The primary complication of diabetes is DFU. Application of deep learning neural network in diagnosing diabetics’ feet can help in the early detection of DFU to prevent severe stage which may lead to amputation. In this paper, AlexNet deep learning neural networks was trained with the plantar thermogram dataset to classify the DFU. In addition, this paper also aims to investigate the effect of greyscale images in the image classification of thermogram on DFU by comparing the accuracy of image classification using colour thermograms and greyscale thermograms. The dataset used consists of 1866 coloured images which 890 images of plantar thermogram with negative DFU and 976 images of foot thermogram with positive DFU. The images were retrieved from Kaggle community with free and full access. In the experiment, data augmentation was performed on the dataset, which the 1866 images were converted into greyscale. As a result, the dataset images were doubled. At the end of this experiment, the improved network achieves an accuracy of 97.8% in classifying the thermograms.

articleTitle: Comparing IOP Measurements in the Iraqi Population: Goldmann Applanation Tonometer vs. Topcon CT-80 Air Puff Tonometer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Accurate measurement of intraocular pressure (IOP) is crucial for diagnosing and managing glaucoma, a sight-threatening condition. This study aimed to compare IOP measurements obtained using Goldmann applanation tonometry (GAT) and Topcon CT-80 air puff tonometer (NCT) in Iraqi patients with varying IOP levels. A total of 98 patients (196 eyes) were included, spanning ages 5 to 80 years, with both genders represented. IOP was measured using both devices, and differences between measurements were analyzed. NCT readings, averaged from three measurements, were taken before GAT to avoid bias. To prevent significant intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction, contact with the applanation probe during GAT was limited to under 5 seconds. Subjects were categorized by age, gender, and IOP range. The mean IOP values obtained by GAT and NCT were 20.56 mmHg and 21.34 mmHg, respectively, with NCT yielding slightly higher readings. Younger age groups demonstrated significant differences between GAT and NCT measurements. Gender-based comparisons showed no significant differences in IOP readings. When stratified by IOP range, NCT overestimated IOP in low and normal ranges but produced similar measurements to GAT in high IOP ranges. Bland-Altman analysis revealed a broad range of agreement between the two devices. The correlation coefficient between GAT and NCT measurements was moderate. In conclusion, the Topcon CT-80 NCT provides easy and comfortable IOP measurement, but it tends to overestimate IOP in low and normal ranges while performing comparably in high IOP ranges. The study recommends caution in interchanging the two modalities due to their wide range of agreement limits.

articleTitle: An Investigation into the Accuracy of Blood Oxygen Saturation Measurement using Smart Watch Devices Among Pediatric Users in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Advancements in technology have led to the development and increased use of biomedical wearable devices equipped with various biosensors. This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of blood oxygen saturation measurements in Saudi pediatric users using the Apple Watch Series 6 and Samsung Galaxy Watch 4. These smartwatches, widely available and relatively affordable fitness trackers, offer the capability to measure blood oxygen saturation and facilitate health monitoring. This paper presents preliminary findings from an investigation into the accuracy of the Apple Watch and Samsung Watch in measuring blood oxygen saturation. Data was collected from a sample of one hundred Saudi pediatric users, comprising 43 females and 57 males, with an average age of 13±3.3 years and a BMI of 21.07±6.3 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Three measurements of blood oxygen saturation were simultaneously recorded using a hospital-grade pulse oximetry machine, as well as the Apple Watch and the Samsung Watch. Statistical comparisons were conducted using a T-test with a significance level of p=0.05, and the results were visualized using Bland-Altman plots. The T-test results indicated a statistically significant difference between the oximeter readings of the smartwatches and the medical-grade oximeter. Additionally, the calculation of errors revealed discrepancies between the measurements obtained from the smartwatches and the hospital-grade oximeter. It was observed that the errors were generally lower in measurements taken from male subjects compared to female subjects. The Bland-Altman plots, considering data from both the Apple Watch and the Samsung Watch, showed moderate agreement between the smartwatches and the hospital pulse oximetry. These findings suggest that while the Apple Watch and Samsung Watch demonstrate potential for measuring blood oxygen saturation, there are discrepancies compared to the accuracy of the hospital-grade oximeter. Further research and refinement may be necessary to improve the precision and reliability of these smartwatches in accurately measuring blood oxygen saturation in pediatric users.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Image Classification: The Purine and Alcohol Intake Awareness over Foods and Drinks for Gout Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: We propose a way to prevent Gout by introducing a method of food image classification that supports detecting rich-purine and alcohol products. We contribute to classifying foods according to their purine and alcohol levels. Hence, the method reduces the chances of hyperuricemia for Gout patients by not consuming them. We investigate the purine and alcohol levels in the food by literature. Our method helps the Gout patient asses the containment in the foods before consuming them. The preliminary results from the research achieved 88.33% accuracy performance. The proposed research is more scientifically documented through a manuscript than similar commercial applications. Hence, its development process and performance are transparent, reliable, repeatable and scientifically proven. This research proposes using Deep Learning to improve the Gout disease problem.

articleTitle: Portable Colposcope Design for Spherical Reflection Removal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Colposcope design is crucial for accurate diagnosis and treatment of cervical abnormalities. Portable colposcope is made to perform a practical examination for cervical cancer. Replaceable and rechargeable batteries are included in this colposcope. As a result, there is no need for an external power source for turning on this colposcope. This makes the colposcope portable. Along with portability, key elements in colposcope design include the optical system and lighting. Specular reflections may be present in the cervical area image and it covers some areas of the cervix. An existing method to reduce specular reflection is image preprocessing. However, with this method, the pixels of the cervical area covered by the specular reflection will be replaced with pixels around the reflection. Consequently, the cervix’s surface area covered by specular reflection is not actual data. This can be solved with a cross-polarizing filter system. Polarizing filter for a colposcope camera is a valuable accessory that removes unwanted reflections and glare during colposcopy procedures. Based on the results, cross polarizing filter on colposcope can reduce light by 92.44%.

articleTitle: Analysis, Monitoring, and Classification System for Apnea in Patients with Down Syndrome
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: According to WHO, Down syndrome is a congenital disorder linked to chromosome 21 that affects 0.1% of the world population. The respiratory system is its weakest point, causing affectations such as Sleep Apnea that can aggravate the problems derived from this syndrome. Sleep-disordered breathing in this population is poorly described. A low-cost system was developed that combines the acquisition of electromyography (EMG) signals from the larynx, respiratory rate, and flow, which are recorded for subsequent analysis. The developed biomedical system is a viable alternative to polysomnography with the advantage of being scalable, the identification and differentiation of General Apneas, Hypopneas, and Obstructive Sleep Apneas (OSA) are achieved with a friendly interface, which allows real-time monitoring of the respiratory parameters of a patient during sleep).

articleTitle: Implementation of Artificial Neural Networks for Grasping Activity Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: A grasping detection system is essential to develop a prosthesis for helping people with disabilities. This study aims to detect grasping activity using an Artificial Neural Network using an Electromyograph sensor. The tool consists of three components: an Electromyograph sensor, an Arduino Nano, and an LED. The Electromyograph sensor detects muscle activity on the lower left arm. There are 5 healthy subject is involved in this study. Data from the subject is acquired and processed on a computer, and the best architecture with the slightest error was selected to be implemented on the Arduino Nano. The weights and biases for the best architecture were entered in the Arduino Nano and then calculated using the new data from the Electromyograph sensor. The average success rate was 88% for the real-time test.

articleTitle: Coherence Analysis of EEG Signal in Happy and Sad Emotions During Visual Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Emotions play a crucial role in human life, influencing various aspects such as thoughts, behavior, and physical health. Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying emotions, particularly sadness, is essential. This study explores the relationship between brain activity associated with sad and happy emotions and the functioning of the left and right hemispheres during visual processing using coherence analysis of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. When the coherence value is low, there is no correlation between the two compared conditions. EEG recordings were obtained from 25 participants using an OpenBCI device, and specific channels (Fp1–Fp2, F7–F8, and O1–O2) related to attention, emotion expression, and visual processing were selected. The recorded data underwent preprocessing to remove artifacts, and subsequent feature extraction was performed using coherence analysis in the gamma sub-band. The results of this study demonstrate alignment with the existing theory that each hemisphere has distinct functions when experiencing feelings of sadness and happiness, as evidenced by the observation of a weak coherence percentage in all hemisphere comparisons between Fp1–Fp2, F7–F8, and O1–O2 (all coherence value is <40%). Another finding in this study is that the human brain works harder when watching sad videos than happy videos. Taking gender into consideration, the research indicates that the male brain is more active under happiness conditions compared to females.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis on a Bionic Foot Prosthesis Model during Walking Gait Phases
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Bionic foot ergonomic quality depends on its design and usage comfortability. Daily activities, sports, and other high-durability required actions are considered in bionic foot design. Bionic foot design is a challenge that has to be overcome to develop ergonomic below-limb prosthetics. Load simulation using Finite Element Method (FEM) can aid bionic foot design development. This study aims to simulate bionic foot design based on gait cycle activities using FEM. Bionic foot design imported into FEM software with load force placed on ground reaction force refers to axial, medial-lateral, and anterior and posterior load. The FEM simulation shows that the loading using the static method with dynamic load is divided into three steps, with the step selection being at three peaks, the first peak is on the side of the most critical peak, the second peak is in the valley, and the third peak is in a critical position which is indicated by the high Ground Reaction Force (GRF), the most extreme angle is at peak 3 with the condition of the feet lifting as high as 21° with a contact pressure of 0.580 MPa with Von-Mises value 0.472.

articleTitle: An Asymmetric Birdcage Coil Design for 19F Lung MR Imaging at 1.5 T
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) based on <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup>F can detect the lung pulmonary ventilation status without radiation and lower cost, which has emerged as a promising approach in the post-COVID era. In this paper, we propose an asymmetric radio frequency (RF) birdcage coil uniquely tailored for <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>H-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup>F lung MR imaging system. This newly designed coil can work nested into the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>H volume coil, thereby enabling simultaneous structural and functional imaging and enhancing patient comfort. After employing conformal mapping to obtain the transformed closed curve, ideal current distributions are directly assigned to finish capacitance calculations, enabling the asymmetric birdcage coil to yield a uniform RF field. The intensity and homogeneity of the produced field are validated by theoretic calculation and electromagnetic simulation. Upon those results, compared to the conventional circular birdcage coil, our novel coil design demonstrates superior performance, establishing its efficacy and superiority.

articleTitle: The Response of Range of Motion Exercise on Upper Extremities Towards Muscle Strength in Critically Ill Patients Using MMT Scale and MyoMES
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Critically ill patients require care aimed at increasing muscle strength. Passive and active Range of Motion (ROM) exercises can be applied on the upper extremities to improve muscle strength, reduce duration of inactivity, increase venous return, increase oxygen distribution towards bodily tissues, and repair muscle dysfunction. Currently, nurses manually conduct muscle strength measurements using a Manual Muscle Test (MMT) scale. CBIOM3S of Universitas Diponegoro designed MyoMES as a technological innovation that aids in measuring muscle strength. This study is Quasi-experimental research with implementing a pre-post-test design with no control group. The participants were four first-day ICU patients with cardiovascular disorders. The participants were intervened with ROM exercise of the upper extremities. On the first day in the ICU, a ROM exercise was performed on the participants, with a pretest using MMT and MyoMES preceding the procedure. The ROM exercise was repeated on the second and third day for 30–60 minutes. The post-test was conducted after the ROM exercise on the third day. MMT and MyoMES were utilised to evaluate the muscle strength of the participants. The data were analysed through the Wilcoxon test. Wilcoxon test revealed no difference in muscle strength measured with MMT and MyoMES between the pretest and the post-test ROM of the right and left wrist flexor and flexor digitorum superficialis muscles for three days.

articleTitle: Enhancing EOG Artifact Removal from EEG Through Independent Component, Band Power, and Pearson’s Correlation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Eye movements introduce artifacts in EEG recordings, thus hindering accurate analysis. To detect and remove electrooculogram (EOG) components from EEG data, we commonly use independent component analysis (ICA). However, existing methods may be inconsistent, thus necessitating better EOG artifact removal. Our study presents an improved EOG artifact removal method that employs band power analysis and Pearson’s correlation coefficient (PCC). This method enhances accuracy and efficiency in identification and removal of EOG artifacts from EEG data. We applied the fast Fourier transform to compute band power (1–2 Hz) for each ICA-derived component. A threshold of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> μV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> identified EOG components with excessive band power. Subsequently, PCC values quantified the impact of each component on EEG channels. This approach accurately pinpointed EOG components for removal. Our proposed method significantly improved EEG signal quality. Combining band power and PCC analysis refined EOG component identification, thus facilitating targeted artifact removal. This method can potentially enhance EEG studies, particularly in eye movement-rich scenarios.

articleTitle: Reverse Engineering Artificial Knee Joint using 3D Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: The knee joints are regarded as one of the parts of the human body in which the thigh bone (femur) to the shin bone (tibia) is linked. The field of engineering involves the processes needed to design, manufacture, assemble, and maintain products and systems. Traditional forward engineering transforms them into physical products or Reverse Engineering (RE) methods. This section presents the methodology and results from the physical experiment on Artificial Knee Joint (AKJ), which was reverse-engineered using a handheld, non-contact 3D laser scanner. The method used compares AKJ coating using tape and AESUB 3D Scanning Spray. The results of measurements with laser scanners are in the form of point clouds. Furthermore, data processing needs to be carried out as an inspection process. AKJ geometry inspection process with 3D laser scanner tool by comparing femoral scan results using tape and AESUB 3D Scanning Spray. This article reported a case study conducted to investigate the possibilities and challenges of 3D scanning technology for reverse engineering. The case study results are compared with those reported in the literature. The technology generally provides opportunities to conduct RE by scanning the object and transforming it into CAD with different surface reconstruction techniques.

articleTitle: Design of Assisted Footwear for Terminal Transverse Lower Limb Deficiency Using Anthropometric Calculations and Forward Engineering Methods: A Study Case
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Implementing a foot prosthesis for transverse hemimelia cases is quite different from amputation cases. Based on case studies, users have deformed feet since birth so they don’t know how to walk using shoes. To train the ability to walk requires the assistance of an adult in walking using a prosthetics leg. The purpose of the research is design of assisted footwear for terminal transverse lower limb deficiency using Anthropometrics and forward engineering methods. The results of product design have applied anthropometry with combine 50th percentile. Therefore, it is necessary to assembly adult Prosthetic Leg and child Prosthetic Leg. The design of the prosthetics leg was designed to suit the case. By using this product, the user will be able to run smoothly.

articleTitle: Atrial Fibrillation Dynamic Features Recognition using 1-D Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a prevalent cardiac arrhythmia that requires accurate detection for effective management and treatment. This study aims to propose a simple yet effective one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) for the AF dynamic features recognition which are extracted using a second-order dynamic system (SODS) concept. The SODS concept utilizes a dynamic system approach to capture the short-term behavior of ECG signals. It employs a second-order differential equation to model the ECG signals based on parameters such as the natural frequency (ω), damping coefficient (ξ), and forcing input (u) to enable the characterization and differentiation of ECG signal. The 1D-CNN model was trained and validated with preprocessed ECG signals from the MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation and MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm database. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the SODS and 1D CNN method for AF recognition. The proposed approach achieves high accuracy, with an accuracy of 98.35% using natural frequency, ω feature.

articleTitle: Monitoring Human Muscle Signal Using Electromyography Sensor Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Muscles serve as a system measure of motion, relaxation, and contraction. The electrical signals generated by muscles during contraction are measured using electrodes connected to electromyography sensors. Electrodes are placed on the surface of the skin to detect electrical signals, which are then used to store condition data based on their placement. Electromyography devices still do not have direct integration through websites or apps, nor are they capable of storing digital patient records. Instead, data collection is done manually or on-site. However, with the Internet of Things-based muscle signal detection device, this process becomes easier for medical personnel. Medical personnel can check the patient’s medical record results through a laptop and save the digital record data. The advantage is that the monitoring process can be done online, so that medical personnel can easily see the patient’s progress from day to day through the available digital data records. The electromyography sensor output is processed by the NodeMCU ESP8266 microcontroller and displayed through the blynk platform integrated with the internet. Electromyograph testing was conducted on the gastrocnemius muscle and 5 different subjects. The test results show that the value of muscle tension is greater when the load treatment has been carried out, both in the biceps muscle and in the gastrocnemius muscle with a large average value in the biceps muscle when the muscle extension condition is 9.746 Volt and 17.296 Volt when the muscle flexion condition. And in the gastrocnemius muscle it is 10.685 Volt when the muscle is in extension and 18.028 Volt when the muscle is in flexion. The value of the voltage is influenced by several factors, one of which is muscle strength and body weight.

articleTitle: Video Stream and Controllable Illuminance for Portable Colposcope
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Portable colposcope is used for diagnosing cervical cancer in Visual Acetic Acid test. It’s used for real-time observation by medical personnel or saved to be predicted by artificial intelligence algorithm. The high cost for the device and the high prevalence of specular reflection found in the generated image inspired us to propose a method for low-cost portable colposcope and specular reflection reduction with real time video streaming and controllable light projection using integrated mobile application. The video streaming using local flask server resulting in 21 FPS of average frame rate and 502 ms latency. The mobile application was capable to interact with the portable colposcope to control the light projection with 0.8 average time latency. The illuminance control was also effective in reducing specular reflection with 0.8 average time latency.

articleTitle: A Motor Imagery-based Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robot System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Patients with motor impairments resulting from brain injuries or neurological disorders often require specialized rehabilitation to regain mobility and function. The primary challenge is ensuring an immersive yet effective rehabilitation experience. Rehabilitation robotics, designed for assisting rehabilitation training process, are beneficial for performing rehabilitation exercises while providing real-time assistance and guidance. These robotics could achieve even better results by capitalizing on patients’ initiative. This work introduces a solution by leveraging Motor Imagery (MI) - a representation of human motor intention - to directly control rehabilitation robotics using brain activities. Specifically, the study showcases the development of a lower limb rehabilitation robot system based on motor imagery, which aims to provide a seamless, immersed rehabilitation experience for patients with motor impairment in lower limb. Three experiments have been conducted in this work: an offline paradigm for data collection and training, a pseudo-online paradigm for quantitative real-time performance analysis, and an online paradigm to evaluate the system’s practical performance in real-world scenarios. The offline paradigm achieved an accuracy of 83% for MI detection and 82.15% for classification. The pseudo-online paradigm demonstrated an accuracy of 66.95%, showing its possible effectiveness in real-time situations. In the online paradigm experiment, participants managed to performance rehabilitation training with this system, but issues with delayed or incorrect response were reported. With enhanced datasets and further optimizations, the combination of MI and rehabilitation robotics can potentially revolutionize the outcomes for patients, offering an immersive and effective rehabilitation experience.

articleTitle: Implementation of Nema-17 Stepper Motor and SG-90 Servo Motor as Mechanical Drivers on Spinal Needle Positioning Test Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Inconsistency in spinal needle visibility is still a problem in the spinal needle insertion method and requires the driver’s accuracy in positioning it based on the angle and depth parameters. The need for accuracy in movement needs to be evaluated with tools and systems that have been made so that they can produce accurate values. This document is presented with software and hardware that supports controlling the Nema-17 stepper motor drive with three axes (X, Y, and Z axes of the test equipment) and the SG-90 servo motor as a spinal needle drive. Based on the position test with the Nema-17 stepper motor, accurate results were obtained using a delay between 100 μs – 500 μs. So, the delay of the driving system does not affect the accurate results. System testing with coordinate input obtained a MAPE value of 14.62%. Whereas for system testing with an input angle between 20°–60° an RMSE value of 0.3 is obtained. So that the algorithms and actuators used in this system succeed in positioning the spinal needle.

articleTitle: Investigation of Ultrasound Wave Behaviour to The Various Materials of 3-Dimensional Printed Cancellous Bone Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Cancellous bone exhibits a porous structure that facilitates cellular adhesion and supports the distribution of growth factors within the bone. Alongside X-ray-based devices commonly employed for assessing bone quality, ultrasound offers a cost-effective, and safe alternative method. However, the utilization of real human bone in ultrasound-based investigations requires careful consideration of ethical aspects, and the challenge of obtaining suitable samples. Moreover, the use of animal bone also presents limitations, as determining the porosity level requires Micro-CT imaging, which can be both expensive and not widely accessible. Hence, this study explores the use of ultrasound to investigate readily available materials in 3D printing as a substitute model for cancellous bone. A bone design with 60% porosity with a hexagonal pattern structure was employed. Ultrasound through transmission (TT) techniques were employed to test and measure the ultrasound parameters such as amplitude, attenuation, and speed of sound (SOS) of seven 3D-printed materials. The result revealed that the ultrasound parameters for Resin material closely approximate the attenuation behaviour of real cancellous bone (1.7 dB/cm), with attenuation values of 1.7358 dB/cm. However, the measured SOS in Resin (1560 m/s) does not adequately reflect the actual SOS in cancellous bone (3800 m/s). As a conclusion, Resin demonstrates promise as a plausible alternative for duplicating cancellous bone in terms of attenuation. However, it may not be suitable for accurately measuring the SOS, highlighting the need for further research and alternative methods.

articleTitle: Using Random Forest and a Hybrid model to Predict Drug Response in Skin Cutaneous Melanoma
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Today, cancer incidence rates continue to rise, but cancer death rates have been declining. This is due in part to early detection and effective treatments, which can further reduce mortality rates. Tailoring therapies to individual patients can further reduce mortality rates, as each patient responds differently to certain drugs. However, the change towards personalized medicine in cancer treatment comes along with some challenges. For instance, the data is extremely high-dimensional, which can lead to classification model overfitting issues. To address this, two machine learning methods were used: Random Forest (RF) and a hybrid model combining RF and Support Vector Machine (RF-SVM). The variables were selected for both methods based on the feature importance obtained from RF. The result shows that in Skin Cutaneous Melanoma (SKCM), RF shows more accurate results than the RF-SVM.

Index Terms: Medicine For The Treatment Of Cancer

articleTitle: Improved Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Network Method to Identify Emphysema in Chest X-Ray Image
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: One of the medical measures to determine the condition of emphysema is to look at the patient’s chest X-ray images manually, but this conventional method has limitations in identifying large amounts of lung X-rays and requires a long time. To reduce the risk of misdiagnosing lung disease, deep learning algorithms are applied. Use of the computer method of the Densenet121 CNN architecture. This method was tested by varying the optimizer and learning rate. The results of the trials found that the Densenet121 architecture was able to identify emphysema accurately with the Adam optimizer at a learning rate of 0.001 and obtained an accuracy of 98.76%, a precision of 98.9%, and a recall of 98.5%.

articleTitle: Thrombus Segmentation in Ultrasound Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) Images using VGG16 and UNet based on Denoising Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) is a disease that occurs when a thrombus forms within the deep veins. This thrombus can disrupt normal blood flow and lead to severe issues if left untreated. The dataset used in this research consists of 2D ultrasound images of thrombus from 5 patients with DVT. Medical specialists used ultrasound equipment to gather and document the dataset. A medical practitioner performed the manual labeling of ultrasound thrombus images. Manual thrombus diagnosis requires a considerable amount of time, and the accuracy of thrombus image analysis relies on specialized doctors. Hence, an automatic thrombus diagnosis is needed for DVT patients to shorten the time and enhance the accuracy of thrombus image analysis. This research proposes thrombus segmentation in ultrasound images using pre-trained VGG16 and UNet model based on denoising filters. The encoder for the UNet model in this segmentation model is a pre-trained VGG16 model. In this study, five denoising filters are utilized. Based on the conducted experiments, the Gaussian filter yielded the most optimal results for thrombus segmentation with an accuracy of 99.166% and a loss value of 0.0269 for the UNet model. Furthermore, the pre-trained VGG16 and UNet model’s accuracy was 99.222%, and the loss value was 0.284. Thrombus prediction tests using the UNet model resulted in a mean IoU of 77.087%, a mean Dice coefficient of 0.8608, and a mean Hausdorff distance of 3.44. Meanwhile, thrombus prediction tests using the pre-trained VGG16 and UNet model produced a mean IoU of 88.298%, a mean Dice coefficient of 0.8784, and a mean Hausdorff distance of 3.07. As a result, utilizing VGG16 as the encoder in the UNet architecture may enhance accuracy when segmenting.

articleTitle: Improving Deep Learning-Based Eye Movements Classification Using Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Eye tracking technology has emerged as a touchless solution for gaze-based object selection, holding immense promise in the field of assistive technology. Despite its potential, accurately classifying various eye movements remains a formidable challenge, critical for dependable object selection. This paper introduces an innovative approach to enhance the performance of deep learning-based eye movements classification. We leveraged Bayesian Optimization (BO) to optimize the Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs), addressing a critical gap in prior research by optimizing hyperparameters. BO, a model-based optimization technique, efficiently explores the hyperparameter search space that leads to significant improvements in classification performance. To rigorously assess our approach, we conducted experiments on the GazeCom dataset, a rich resource annotated for diverse eye movements with a specific emphasis on smooth pursuit that is vital for calibration-free eye tracking applications. Using a lighter model, our approach significantly improved the classification of different types of eye movements—including fixation, saccade, and smooth pursuit. This result outperformed the baseline TCNs model by a margin of 1% to 7.21%. A notable improvement was observed in the classification result of smooth pursuit eye movement (F1 score: 0.8346). This achievement marks a decisive step toward refining the performance of assistive technology based on gaze interaction. Furthermore, our study can be used as a guide for future implementation of hyperparameters optimization in deep learning-based eye movements classification.

articleTitle: VR and Exoskeleton Assisted Lower Limb Rehabilitation based on Motor Imagery BCI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Motor imagery (MI) enhances rehabilitation in brain-injured patients by leveraging neuroplasticity to rebuild neuron connections. Combining MI with exoskeleton robotics and virtual reality (VR) can further improve recovery outcomes. In this study, we integrated a lower limb exoskeleton robot (MAX-1), the Oculus Quest 2 VR headset, and an MI-BCI system. Patients, equipped with the exoskeleton and VR headset, undertake motor imagery tasks, resulting in the exoskeleton robot’s movements guided by EEG signals from the Emotiv EPOC Flex headset. These EEG signals are processed and transformed into leg commands, with concurrent feedback provided in the VR environment. The research comprises three experiments: an offline experiment for primary data collection and training, a pseudo online experiment for simulating real-time processing, and an online serious game experiment to assess the system’s real-world applicability. The offline experiment showed an EEGNet model accuracy of 85.2% for MI detection and 78.3% for classification. The pseudo online experiment achieved an accuracy of 67.2%, indicative of its potential in a real-time scenario. In the online serious game experiment, while participants were able to complete the game, challenges in game control were reported, underscoring areas for future enhancement.

articleTitle: Optimization Fused Deposition Modeling Parameter of Interference Screw using Full Factorial Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Interference screws are one of the most common and widely used fixing techniques in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction. Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) is one of the most commonly used methods in additive manufacturing engineering that can be used to manufacture interference screws. Setting the process parameters of FDM for each material used significantly impacts the quality of the product. This paper aims to investigate and optimize the process factors of FDM most affecting interference screw density and torsion. The effect of process factors, including nozzle temperature, layer height, nozzle diameter, print speed, and infill percentage on the interference screw, was calculated statistically by the full factorial design (FFD) design process. The optimized FDM process parameter was a nozzle temperature of 195 °C, a layer height of 0.12 mm, a nozzle diameter of 0.4 mm, a print speed of 40 mm/s, and an infill percentage of 25%. The results supported by statistical analysis can help future research on designing and manufacturing interference screws.

articleTitle: The Effect of Virtual Reality-based on Intervention in Stroke Patients: Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: In the elderly, the most common cause of disability is stroke. The current development of digital technology has brought advancements in stroke therapy exercises. Nowadays, many researchers and healthcare professionals are starting to use Virtual Reality (VR) as a new technology to implement innovative therapy exercises in training stroke patients. This review evaluates the effectiveness of using VR in the therapy process to enhance the motoric abilities of stroke patients. This review was conducted on research articles published between 2010 and 2023, meeting the inclusion criteria from PubMed, Scopus, IEEE, and Science Direct. Stroke patients showed significant improvements across various cognitive domains. 20 studies were found to meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria. The selected studies examined the impact of VR on the stroke therapy process or compared VR therapy with conventional therapy. The results show that VR has the potential to help stroke patients when undergoing rehabilitation, where patients experience significant improvements in various domains of motor function. VR therapy with its methodology is effective in improving upper/lower extremity movement, quality of life, postural balance, and reducing stress and depression levels in stroke patients. VR can be implemented both as a standalone therapy or as an addition to conventional therapy methods.

articleTitle: Building a Simple COVID-19 Knowledge Graph in Bahasa Indonesia: A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: COVID-19 is an acute respiratory disease that has become a pandemic worldwide. Many studies have been conducted to enhance our understanding of COVID-19. However, the abundance of information obtained from these studies has resulted in information overload. In this study, we purposed a simple COVID-19 Knowledge Graph in Bahasa Indonesia as a way to reconstruct knowledge to combat this information overload. We used Bahasa Indonesia in our study to explore its potential for constructing a Knowledge Graph (KG). The construction of our KG involved manual curation of medical literatures and annotation of entities and relationships by the domain experts. The KG was implemented using Neo4J version 5. We successfully demonstrated our COVID-19 KG, which consists of 240 nodes and 276 relationships with 15 and 14 node and relationship labels, respectively. Accessing the information within the KG is made effortless through the use of Cypher queries in Neo4J. Further research is still needed to develop the KG into a larger and better one. However, our COVID-19 KG can serve as a basis for further development.

articleTitle: Detection of Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS) in Static Cycling Exercise Using Multilayer Perceptron Neural Network (MLPNN)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Static cycling is a convenient and widely accessible form of exercise, with spinning being a popular indoor cycling workout using specialized stationary bikes. However, spinning comes with some risks, including the potential for exertional rhabdomyolysis (ER), known explicitly as spinning-induced ER (SIER). There have been 46 reported cases of SIER, which involves the breakdown of muscle tissue and can lead to symptoms like fatigue, nausea, muscle pain, and organ dysfunction. Detecting Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS), one of the symptoms of rhabdomyolysis, can help diagnose SIER early. To achieve this, a study was conducted using Electromyograph (EMG) sensors placed on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves muscles of healthy young male subjects (20–22 years old) during sprint interval cycling (SIC) exercise. The EMG signals were analyzed in time and frequency domains to extract relevant parameters. Subjective testing was also done using the Likert Scale of Muscle Soreness questionnaire as a reference. The study proposed a Multilayer Perceptron Neural Network (MLPNN) classification method for DOMS detection, achieving an impressive accuracy of 94.2% and a loss value of 6.7%. These findings indicate the system’s effectiveness in objectively identifying DOMS in individuals participating in static bicycle exercise.

articleTitle: Comparison of EEG Oscillations During Visual Memory Encoding and Recognition under Exposure to Mozart’s Sonata Music K448
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Classical Mozart’s music may provide a benefit or drawback effect on memory performance. Hence, an experimental study was conducted to discover its influence on memorizing ability. The evaluation indicator based behavioral data is common and cannot describe the effect of stimulation on body responses. The recent work investigates the influence of Mozart’s Sonata K448 music on visual working memory. The indicators of behavioral data and brain activities were used to assess memory performance. The brain signal was recorded from 60 participants via an electroencephalography (EEG) machine of 10–20 electrode system placement during visual assessment encoding and recognition stages. The duration of the assessment was 120 seconds for each stage. The acquired EEG signal was pre-processed using a wavelet filter to remove contaminated undesired components. Then, it was decomposed into theta, alpha, beta, and gamma oscillations. The mean, maximum amplitude and relative power were obtained from each oscillation. The EEG features pattern elucidated that brain activity was higher in recognition than encoding stages. Listening to Mozart’s music during visual assessment increased certain features compared to the control condition. In remark, Mozart’s music positively influenced visual memory.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic-Based Liquid Level Measurement in Dynamic Dialysate Preparation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Instrumentation for an intelligent ultrasonic liquid level measurement system was developed. This system was based on the measurement of the time of flight of ultrasonic pulses generated from the surface of the ultrasonic transducer reflected from the liquid surface, and received by the ultrasonic transducer. The system consists of an ultrasonic sensor, temperature and humidity sensor (SHT11), analog front end (TDC1000-Q1), digital back end, serial communication interface, and buzzer. The Analog front end (TDC1000-Q1) consists of pulser and receiver circuitry. The digital back end consists of an ARM Cortex M4 microcontroller for controlling pulse reception frequencies, processing the echo signals, and acquiring the temperature and humidity data from the SHT11 device. Further processing for determining the liquid level based on the ultrasonic liquid level measured data, and temperature and humidity of the air was conducted on the personal computer. The experimental work was conducted on water containers made from plexiglass and stainless steel with various water temperatures and humidities. The results show that close agreements are observed between the water’s real height and the ultrasonic technique for water temperatures less than 30°C. However, as water temperature increases, discrepancies at less than 5% in water level measurement were observed between the water’s real height and the ultrasonic measurement.

articleTitle: Improving the Effectiveness of Telemedicine Services: A Conceptual Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: The use of telemedicine to provide healthcare services is an approach that has experienced a rapid increase in use in recent years. Telemedicine will significantly increase efficiency in using resources when providing and obtaining healthcare services. However, in terms of effectiveness, the provision of healthcare services through the telemedicine system still falls short compared to the effectiveness of in-person healthcare services, which still require further improvement. This study uses the literature review method to understand the factors influencing the effectiveness of healthcare services provided within the telemedicine system. The results of this review suggest that information technology infrastructure, telemedicine application quality, regulations related to telemedicine, and the capabilities of physicians providing healthcare services in the telemedicine system are crucial to enhancing the effectiveness of telemedicine service. This study provides a framework for telemedicine service providers to improve the effectiveness of healthcare services for their patients.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Edge-Preservation based Normalized Convolution for Medical Image Enhancement and Noise Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Acquired medical images often contain noise due to various factors that affect image quality. The noisy image indicates the presence of inappropriate information or loss of original information due to changes in the pixel values. For diagnosis purposes, the acquired or noisy medical image needs to be reconstructed to obtain an enhanced image or denoised image for a better decision. One of the techniques to enhance or reduce the noise can be performed by normalized convolution to interpolate the change of pixels in the original image. This paper is presented to investigate the feasibility of the normalized convolution filter to enhance and reduce medical image noise. The study was performed through experiments using several types of medical images, namely Brain MRI, Breast Ultrasound, Chest X-ray, Retinal OCT, Mammogram, and RSNA Bone Age images. Experimental results show that the normalized convolution could produce an enhanced image with sharper contrast. In the image enhancement, the enhanced image obtained by this filter achieves 41.12 dB on the PSNR average. In the medical image denoising, the normalized convolution could produce better visual quality to reduce the Gaussian, Salt & Pepper, Poisson, and Speckle with PSNR averages are 28.43dB, 32.82dB, 32.49dB, and 29.30dB. This method also outperforms basic image denoising filters, such as Imbox, Wiener, and Median Filterings. Hence, this filter could be used as an alternative for medical image preprocessing, such as image enhancement and noise reduction.

articleTitle: AI-based Paediatric Teledermatology Analysis and Proposed Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Biomedical Instrumentation and Technology Conference (IBITeC)
abstract: Teledermatology technology development has been increasing due to the pandemic of COVID-19 which limit human physical contact. In addition, it is designed to cope with the unbalanced distribution of dermatologists especially in rural country including Indonesia. It implies that the dermatology health care are provided by general practitioners. The competence of general practitioners in dealing with dermatological diseases is limited. Therefore, the probability of misdiagnosis cases is considerably high. The misdiagnosis will delay the recovery which will affect the quality of life. Specifically for paediatric cases, misdiagnosis could affect the child’s growth and development. Connecting the general practitioner to the specialist or consultant and supporting them with AI-based technology through teledermatology technology becomes urgent due to these issues. This paper aims to present a literature review on the development of teledermatology worldwide with its scope and objectives. The PRISMA flowchart method is used to outline the effectiveness of the teledermatology system and its features. The presented literature review provides insight into the urgency of teledermatology system in each country, framework modelling and significant features. In addition, this paper contributes to propose paediatric teledermatology design in Indonesia based on the local background and insight of recent teledermatology technology development point of views.
